price_per_million.source: openrouter.ai/models, confirmed via preflight 2026-11-11; thinking tokens billed as output

research_concepts: play-type possession records derived from play-by-play
methodological_questions: Does adherence to the recommended mix predict winning after controlling for team quality and opponent strength?
Is the recommended mix derived from data that overlap the outcome it is meant to predict?
Are 54 series enough for the effect size seen earlier?
How reliable is the play-type tagging, and is it biased for some play types (e.g. CUT, PNR)?
How should multiplicity across adherence definitions and thresholds be handled?

historical_evidence.finding: Series-level AVOID share vs winning. Game-level rho=-0.19, p=0.008, with inflated n and a team-quality confound. Series-level rho=-0.26, p=0.07 at n=50, underpowered (~80 series stated as needed for p<0.05). The low AVOID-share bin won 52.6% vs 37.0% for the 25-50% bin. Still confounded by team quality (OKC disciplined and good). Verdict recorded: inconclusive.

Descriptive conformance of observed mix to the recommended opener in 4 playoff G1s (8 offensive sides). Average |delta| ranged 4.5pp to 24.0pp by leverage bucket. 4 of 8 sides best matched opener #3, not rank-1. CUT and PNR were muted by the tagger floor. Single-game horizon, no outcome comparison.

LLM counter selection vs deterministic BEST tier, n=3 triggers. The agent agreed with BEST 1/3 and picked AVOID 2/3. Mean H2 PPP was BEST 1.650, agent 1.154, AVOID 0.642. The record says 230+ disagreements are needed. Verdict recorded: inconclusive.

Ranked playsheet validation on 10 series. Spearman rho=-0.0639, p=0.0997, n=665, no clear full-rank signal. Kruskal-Wallis p=2.7e-05. Pairwise Mann-Whitney BEST 1.257 PPP (n=56) vs AVOID 1.092 (n=160), p=0.004. Trigger accuracy rho=0.4525, n=121. Limited by leakage, low measurement reliability and small sample, with drift/nonstationarity listed as a risk. The record text was cut off in the retrieval result.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Series-level association of AVOID share with winning, at game level and at series level (n=50)
failed_approaches.why: Recorded as A_unanswerable. Limited by confounding (team quality) and small sample; the game-level result had inflated n.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Comparing LLM counter choice to the BEST tier on H2 PPP
failed_approaches.why: Only n=3 triggers; the record says 230+ disagreements are needed (small sample).
No clear full-rank signal. Limits recorded: leakage, low measurement reliability, small sample.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Conformance measurement of observed vs recommended mix
failed_approaches.why: Mechanical floor (CUT and PNR muted by the tagger), single-game horizon, no outcome comparison.

evidence_establishes: A series-level AVOID-share vs winning test on n=50 gave rho=-0.26, p=0.07, in the hypothesised direction but not significant, and the record states it remains confounded by team quality (FAM:SF-CHT-039).
The record states ~80 series are needed for p<0.05 at that effect size (FAM:SF-CHT-039).
A pairwise BEST>AVOID difference in H2 PPP was recorded, but the same study found no clear full-rank signal and flagged leakage and measurement-reliability limits (FAM:SF-APPS-018).
Observed play-type mixes diverge from the recommended opener by 4.5 to 24.0 percentage points in a small descriptive sample, and CUT/PNR are muted by the tagger (FAM:SF-APPS-017).
evidence_does_not_establish: That adherence to a recommended mix predicts winning independent of team quality: the only outcome-linked record is confounded and non-significant.
That the recommended mix is valid out of sample: the validation record lists leakage as a limitation.
Anything about the exact adherence metric in this question. FAM:SF-CHT-039 used AVOID share, a related but different exposure.
Any effect on series outcomes with 54 series (not 80), or with a mix defined strictly from pre-outcome information.
own_inferences: With n=54 and a true rho near -0.26, power at alpha=0.05 is roughly 45-55%, so a null would be uninformative.
Strong teams probably adhere more because they have more shot-making and talent, so a raw positive association is likely to be confounded by quality.
If the recommended mix is fit on the same games or series it is scored against, any association is partly mechanical (outcome-derived label and leakage).
The better design is game-level within series: it uses far more observations, and series fixed effects remove team-quality differences, provided the mix is built only from prior games.
FAM:SF-APPS-018 (n=665 alternatives, 10 series) suggests an effect at the possession or alternative level may be detectable even if series-level winning is not. That is a different estimand.
uncertainties: How the 'suppression-conditional recommended mix' is computed (training window, whether outcomes enter it) is not stated.
The 54 series may include partial 2025-26 playoffs (complete only from 2026-06-21), so the sample is not final.
The full text of FAM:SF-APPS-018 was cut, so its validation and leakage details are unknown.
Tagger reliability for CUT/PNR and any drift across seasons are unquantified.
The earlier 50 series may overlap the current 54, so they are not independent confirmation.

historical_effect.explanation: Without history I might have proceeded with a plain series-level correlation. The records show a near-identical series-level test at n=50 was underpowered and confounded (needing ~80 series), and that validation was marred by leakage and measurement limits. I therefore moved to proceed_with_changes: a game-level, series-fixed-effects design with strictly out-of-sample recommendations, and series-level analysis only as secondary and descriptive.

blocking_constraints.text: 54 series gives about 50% power for rho≈0.26, and prior work states ~80 series are needed.
Team quality drives both adherence and winning, so series-level results cannot be read causally without within-series or quality-adjusted designs.
The recommended mix must be defined without using the outcome or the games being scored, or the association is circular.

prior_work.summary: A close AVOID-share vs series-winning test at n=50 was inconclusive (rho=-0.26, p=0.07, confounded). Adherence itself was only described at game level, and playsheet validation was mixed with leakage and reliability caveats. The question as posed is not answered.

risks.text: 54 series is below the ~80 recorded as needed; the series-level test is likely inconclusive.
Good teams adhere more and win more (the OKC example in FAM:SF-CHT-039); opponent strength and home court also matter.
If the recommended mix or its suppression triggers use H2 or later same-series data, the adherence score contains future information. FAM:SF-APPS-018 lists leakage.
Best/avoid tiers derived from PPP outcomes make adherence partly a proxy for scoring success.
Tagger errors and muted CUT/PNR (FAM:SF-APPS-017, FAM:SF-APPS-018) add noise to adherence and bias it toward the null.
Floors in the tagger for some play types cap the achievable adherence.
Many ways to define adherence (distance metric, tier, leverage weighting, window) inflate false positives unless one is fixed in advance.
Play-type mix and tagging may differ across 2022-23 to 2025-26, so pooled estimates need season effects.
Series-level win rates are structured (favourites win most), so a naive accuracy comparison is misleading.

design.estimand: Within-series association between a game's adherence score (distance of observed offensive play-type mix to the pre-registered recommended mix, from prior-games information only) and that game's win probability, adjusted for team quality and opponent strength. Secondary: series-level association between mean adherence and series win.
design.unit: Primary: team-game within series (each game contributes two sides). Secondary: series (n=54, or the final count once 2025-26 playoffs complete).
design.sample: NBA playoff games 2022-23 to 2025-26 (54 series). Freeze the sample when the 2025-26 playoffs are complete (from 2026-06-21), or declare partial series explicitly. Exclude games with too few possessions or missing play-by-play. Optional extension to the regular season with the same rules for more power.
design.power: Series-level with n=54: ~50% power for |rho|=0.26, so treat as secondary and descriptive; a non-significant result is inconclusive and not evidence of no effect. Primary game-level test with series fixed effects: simulate or compute power for odds ratio ~1.1 per SD adherence, with cluster-robust SEs by series, and report the minimum detectable effect before looking at outcomes.
design.controls: Pre-game team strength (net rating or Elo using only games before the series), opponent strength, home court, series fixed effects in the primary model, season effects, game-level possession count and pace. Recommended mix built strictly from earlier games or from other seasons, with no outcome from the scored game or any later game. Fix the suppression-trigger rule, tier definitions and distance metric in advance. Sensitivity: exclude CUT and PNR given the tagger floor.
design.falsification: Placebo adherence to a randomised or shuffled recommended mix from other series (should give null). Negative control: adherence to the mix recommended to a different opponent or series. Time-reversal check: adherence computed from later games must not outperform prior-game adherence. If the effect disappears under series fixed effects or quality adjustment, report it as confounded by team quality.
design.multiplicity: One primary adherence metric and one primary model are fixed in advance. Alternative metrics, thresholds and subsets are labelled exploratory, with Holm or Benjamini-Hochberg correction across the pre-listed set.
design.decision_rule: Supported if the primary game-level coefficient has the hypothesised sign, cluster-robust p<0.05 (one pre-registered primary test), survives the quality adjustment, and passes the placebo and negative-control checks. Rejected only if the 95% CI excludes the minimum effect of interest (the pre-registered OR 1.1). Otherwise inconclusive. The series-level result cannot by itself support or reject.
design.data_version: NBA stats API per-game files and derived play-type graph for 2022-23 to 2025-26. Freeze a snapshot after the 2025-26 playoffs complete (2026-06-21 or later); record the tagger version, extraction date and the series list in the pre-registration.

methodological_questions: Does adherence to a recommended play-type mix predict game or series wins?
How is the recommended mix derived and is it fit on the same outcomes it predicts (leakage/outcome-derived label)?
Is 54 series enough power, and how do confounding by team quality and opponent strength affect adherence-win association?
How reliable is play-type classification and suppression measurement, and is there regression to the mean or multiple testing across play types?
args.query: adherence to suppression-conditional recommended play-type mix predicts winning in playoff series; defensive suppression best/avoid counter strategy

system_prompt:
You are a basketball analytics researcher deciding whether and how a research question should be studied.
You work only from the task statement and the tools listed below. Do not assume facts you have not seen.

The work has two stages, in this order.
Stage 1, retrieval:
1. Read the research objective and the data description.
2. Identify the research concepts and methodological questions the task raises.
3. Retrieve historical evidence by calling retrieve_history.
In stage 1 do not assess the question, predict outcomes or decide. Your only stage-1 reply is the retrieve_history call.
Stage 2, assessment, after the retrieval result is returned:
4. Summarise the relevant historical findings and failed approaches.
5. State what the historical evidence does and does not establish.
6. Assess whether the research question is testable.
7. Identify methodological risks and potential confounders.
8. Make the final research decision.
9. Explain whether and how the historical evidence changed the decision.
The stage-2 output format is given together with the retrieval result.

Evidence rules: keep what a retrieved record states (historical_evidence and failed_approaches, each citing the
identifier of a returned record and its status exactly as recorded) separate from your own inference and from
uncertainty or missing information. Cite only identifiers returned by a tool, and never describe an earlier study that
no tool returned. In some settings retrieval returns no records; then state that no historical evidence was available.

Tools:
- retrieve_history(research_concepts, methodological_questions, query): the prescribed retrieval step. Returns the most relevant consolidated study-family records of earlier research by this project that are available in this setting, with their identifiers; returns an empty list when none are available.
- glossary(): definitions of basketball and project terms used in task statements.
- data_catalog(): the fields available in each per-game data file.
- search_documents(query): rank further study-family documents by text relevance; returns up to 4 families not yet returned.
- read_family(id): the complete record of one study family (for example 'FAM:SF-APPA-001').

Protocol: every reply is exactly one JSON object and nothing else.
To call a tool: {"action": "tool", "tool": "<name>", "args": {...}}
To finish (stage 2 only): {"action": "final", "output": <object following the stage-2 schema>}
You may call at most 12 tools; then you must finish. Check that every opening brace has a closing brace.

Risk codes (use only these): SAMPLE_SIZE_POWER, EXPOSURE_SPARSITY, MEASURE_RELIABILITY, RTM_SELECTION, OUTCOME_DERIVED_LABEL, LEAKAGE_LOOKAHEAD, MECHANICAL_FLOOR, BASE_RATE, CONFOUNDING, LABEL_ERROR, PLACEBO_DEPENDENCE, MULTIPLE_TESTING, IMPLEMENTATION_BUG, DRIFT_NONSTATIONARITY

Research question (as posed on 2026-06-16, in the area of defensive suppression and counter strategy (best/avoid)):
Adhering to a suppression-conditional recommended mix predicts winning.

Data available on that date:
- NBA 2022-23 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2023-24 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2024-25 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2025-26 regular season (complete from 2026-04-13; partial before)
- NBA 2025-26 playoffs (complete from 2026-06-21; partial before)
- Sources: Per-game files from the NBA stats API: play-by-play (action type, sub-type, clock, period, score, player, shot distance and result), substitution rotation intervals, starters, defensive matchup minutes and partial possessions, box-score summary. Derived play-type possession records (initiator, play type, points) in a graph database built from the play-by-play.
- Units available to a study of this question (as recorded): 54 series

Your job is to decide, before any analysis is run, whether this question can be answered with this data, what has already been established about it, which methodological and statistical risks threaten a test of it, and either a pre-registration-quality design or a reasoned recommendation not to proceed.

reasoning_details.text:
I'm weighing whether to pull up FAM:SF-APPS-018 to check the cut text, but the budget allows it and it isn't strictly needed, so I'll lean toward finalizing and noting the cut. On the units, I have 54 series, and the earlier estimate of about 80 needed for p<0.05 at rho -0.26 means I'm short of that threshold.

The series count is 54, a bit above the roughly 50 I had before, and the data appears to include partial 2025-26 playoff results since the question was posed before those rounds finished. I'm weighing a design that uses game-level data with fixed effects and a mix defined only from prior games, and I'm estimating power at around 45-50% for rho 0.26 at this sample size, so I'm leaning toward proceed_with_changes.
